posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
I've split this off to keep from spinning off the relief topic.

[http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/v ... php?t=3937](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3937)

Technically it's a trademark that I'm running the risk of infringing. Copyright only covers tangible works.

Given that they don't offer their own versions of these holograms (or any that I'm aware of) and that I'm such small-fry (I've only sold one of these so far) I'm not too worried about harming the trademark holders by stealing profits from them or diluting their work. I'm not claiming that they are "official" holograms but rather my own work.

I know this is a grey area (possibly very dark grey) and if they ever said "stop" I would.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
They can go after you with a great deal of force. However they can not recover much money. First they would give you a Cease and Desist. Then they would try to sue you for lost income they could have made and try to tack on punitive damages. 

If you start making $100s a week on licensed products you will hear from attorneys.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
This does raise some good questions...

If the volume is low, is it better to ask for forgiveness rather than risk being told "no" when asking for permission? The word "better" is certainly open to interpretation and I welcome anyones constructive input. There are certainly moral implications. 

Also, how low is "low"? Using me as an example I've made several master holograms using licensable imagery and can make copies for sale or gifts without much trouble. I've given away some to friends and family and have sold a total of three of them. It can be argued that three sales haven't hurt the license holders one bit and I can (I think rightfully) argue that I'm not likely to do any volume that would ever show up on their balance sheets either as a negative (non-licensed) or as a positive (licensed).

On the other hand, I also haven't invited them to participate in the potential profit-making by seeking out a license. I certainly can't argue that's the "right" way to go about it.
